criteria.reason: The student provides a basic definition of a data structure, but it lacks depth and clarity.
The student provides a comprehensive list of types of data structures, including linear and non-linear data structures.
The student provides examples of data structures, including array, linked list, stack, queue, tree, and graph.
The student provides a clear explanation of the characteristics of non-linear data structures, including tree and graph.
The student answer provides a clear definition of an algorithm, aligning with the provided text.
The student answer lists and briefly describes the characteristics of a good algorithm, including well-defined inputs, outputs, finiteness, effectiveness, determinism, and language independence.
The student answer does not provide specific examples of the characteristics of a good algorithm.

The student correctly defined complexity analysis as a technique to characterise the time taken by an algorithm with respect to input size.
The student correctly identified three types of complexity analysis: Best time complexity, Average time complexity, and Worst time complexity.
The student correctly defined Time Complexity as the time complexity of an algorithm quantifying the amount of time taken by an algorithm to run as a function of the length of the input.
The student mentioned Space Complexity as the amount of memory required by the algorithm to solve a given problem, but did not provide a specific example.
The student correctly defined an array as a linear data structure that stores elements of the same data type in contiguous memory locations.
The student correctly defined a linked list as a linear data structure consisting of nodes, where each node contains data and a reference to the next node.
The student correctly identified that linked lists have a forward reference to the next node.
The student incorrectly stated that arrays have a fixed size after creation.
The student correctly stated that linked lists can grow or shrink dynamically.
